events.title: Argentina's Penalty & Messi Goal
events.description: Denzel Dumfries fouls Marcos Acuña inside the penalty box; Lionel Messi converts the penalty kick to put Argentina ahead 2–0.
events.quickNote: Acuña was fouled inside the Netherlands penalty area. Messi scored the penalty to put Argentina 2–0 ahead.
facts: Denzel Dumfries committed a foul on Marcos Acuña inside the Netherlands penalty area at match minute 70:40.
Referee Antonio Mateu Lahoz awarded a direct penalty kick to Argentina.
Lionel Messi scored the penalty into the bottom-right corner at minute 72:39.

events.title: Netherlands Score: Weghorst Header
events.description: Substitute Wout Weghorst scores a glancing header from Steven Berghuis's curling cross to pull the Netherlands back to 2–1.
events.quickNote: Weghorst had just come on. Berghuis crossed from the right, and Weghorst headed in to make it 2–1.
facts: Wout Weghorst was brought on as a substitute for Memphis Depay at match minute 77:57.
Steven Berghuis delivered a curling cross from the right flank.
Weghorst scored with a glancing header into the far corner at match minute 82:17.
uncertainty: Tactical instructions given by Netherlands coach Louis van Gaal during the substitution are not recorded in official match data.

events.title: Paredes Foul, Bench Incident & Caution
events.description: Leandro Paredes fouls Nathan Aké and kicks the ball into the Dutch dugout; Virgil van Dijk pushes him down as a mass altercation breaks out.
events.quickNote: Paredes fouled Aké, then kicked the ball toward the Dutch bench. A confrontation followed, and Paredes was booked. The report does not say exactly which action led to the card.
facts: Leandro Paredes challenged Nathan Aké near the touchline at match minute 87:57.
Immediately after the whistle, Paredes kicked the loose ball with force into the Netherlands technical area.
Virgil van Dijk charged forward and shoved Paredes to the pitch, triggering a confrontation between both benches.
Referee Antonio Mateu Lahoz cautioned Paredes with a yellow card at the 89th minute.
uncertainty: Official records do not state whether the referee cautioned Paredes specifically for the foul on Aké, kicking the ball at the dugout (unsporting behaviour), or inciting the confrontation.

events.title: Netherlands Equalise: Disguised Free Kick
events.description: In the 101st minute, Teun Koopmeiners takes an ingenious short free kick through the defensive wall to Wout Weghorst, who turns and scores to equalise 2–2.
events.quickNote: Koopmeiners rolled the free kick to Weghorst instead of shooting. Weghorst turned and scored to make it 2–2.
facts: Referee added 10 minutes of stoppage time, extending past the 100th minute due to stoppages and altercations.
Netherlands were awarded a direct free kick on the edge of the Argentine penalty area.
Rather than shooting over the defensive wall, Teun Koopmeiners rolled a disguised low pass past the wall to Wout Weghorst.
Weghorst held off Lisandro Martínez and slotted the finish into the bottom corner at match minute 100:32 to make it 2–2.

events.title: Extra Time Ends 2–2: Advances to Shootout
events.description: After 30 minutes of extra time the score remains 2–2; FIFA World Cup knockout regulations dictate that the winner is decided by a penalty shootout.
events.quickNote: The score was still 2–2 after extra time, so the winner had to be decided by a penalty shootout.
facts: Neither side scored during the two 15-minute extra time periods.
Under FIFA World Cup knockout rules, drawn matches after extra time proceed immediately to kicks from the penalty mark (shootout).
Both teams submitted kick orders and referee conducted the coin toss to select the goal and first kicking team.

events.title: Argentina Win Shootout 4–3 & Dumfries Red Card
events.description: Emiliano Martínez saves two penalties; Lautaro Martínez converts the winning kick (4–3). Denzel Dumfries receives his second caution and is sent off during post-shootout tension.
events.quickNote: Argentina won the shootout 4–3. Dumfries received a second caution and was sent off after the decisive kick; it did not change the result.
facts: Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez saved the Netherlands' first two kicks taken by Virgil van Dijk and Steven Berghuis.
Lautaro Martínez scored Argentina's fifth penalty to secure a 4–3 shootout victory.
Denzel Dumfries was cautioned twice during the shootout phase (officially recorded at 128' and 129') and shown a red card for two bookable offences.
Dumfries's dismissal occurred as the shootout was concluding and did not affect Argentina's victory.
uncertainty: Broadcast footage shows multiple Argentine and Dutch players clashing near the centre circle immediately following the winning kick; the referee's match report does not detail the specific verbal exchange that resulted in Dumfries's second caution.
